rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The no-tanwīn reading can be understood as suppressing intended tanwīn at a meeting of two vowelless consonants, without changing the meaning.
rows.anchor: أحدهما أن يكون القارىء له أراد التنوين ، ثم حذفه لالتقاء الساكنين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second analysis treats ibn as an adjective and posits an omitted element in the clause.
rows.anchor: والوجه الثاني : أن يكون الابن صفة ، ويكون التنوين قد سقط

rows.speaker: منهم
rows.claim: One reported analysis supplies an omitted subject, yielding ‘the Jews said: he is Ezra, son of God.’
rows.anchor: فمنهم من جعله مبتدأ ، فقدر ' وقالت اليهود هو عزير ابن الله '

rows.speaker: منهم
rows.claim: Another reported analysis supplies an omitted predicate, yielding ‘the Jews said: Ezra, son of God, is our deity.’
rows.anchor: ومنهم من جعله خبرا ، فقدر وقالت اليهود : ' عزير ابن الله معبودنا '

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The adjectival parse is untenable: denial or affirmation applies to the predicate, while an adjective remains established even in a negated sentence, wrongly removing sonship from the denial.
rows.anchor: وإذا كان الأمر كذلك كان جعل الابن صفة في الآية ، مؤديا إلى الأمر العظيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A present-tense verb linked by wāw to a past event can narrate that event in the past rather than describe a simultaneous state; the present form vividly depicts one action.
rows.anchor: فليست الواو فيها للحال ، وليس المعنى : نجوت راهنا مالكا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The vivid present depicts one part of the scene while leaving the other report in its ordinary past form; the report about Ibn ʿAtīk illustrates the same usage.
rows.anchor: أن يحكي الحال في أحد الخبرين ، ويدع الآخر على ظاهره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When a negative particle precedes the present tense, the construction changes: examples occur both with wāw and without it.
rows.anchor: فإن دخل حرف نفي على المضارع تغير الحكم فجاء بالواو وبتركها كثيرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The poem suppresses understood objects after four verbs, making them seem untransitive and concentrating attention on asserting the actions themselves.
rows.anchor: فيها حذف مفعول مقصود قصده في أربعة مواضع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Leaving the object unexpressed generalizes the effect: a situation of this kind would weary any mother, despite maternal patience; naming ‘us’ would restrict the claim.
rows.anchor: يتضمن أن من حكم مثله في كل أم تمل وتسأم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘Chambers that warmed and shaded’ describes chambers whose nature is to provide warmth and shade; adding an explicit object would destroy that general sense.
rows.anchor: حجرات من شأن مثلها أن تدفىء وتظل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The omitted object can convey both focus on the action and a general quality that would be lost if the object were stated.
rows.anchor: توفير العناية على إثبات الفعل ، والدلالة على أن القصد من ذكر الفعل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage singles out خسأت as the word under examination in the Bedouin couplet.
rows.anchor: المقصود : لفظة ' خسأت '

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The dawn is said to ‘give permission’ to see because daylight makes sight possible after night had prevented it.
rows.anchor: لما كان تعذر الإبصار منعا من الليل ، جعل إمكانه عند ظهور الصبح إذنا من الصبح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jurjani calls the couplet quoted by al-Jāḥiẓ exceptionally beautiful and points to Bashshār’s related image of carrying a burdensome companion like a boil beneath a skin patch.
rows.anchor: ومما هو في غاية الحسن ، وهو من الفن الأول قول الشاعر ؛ أنشده الجاحظ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The metaphor ‘bridge’ has unequal force across its uses: it is more beautiful for toil as a bridge to comfort than in the first example, with a further use by Rabīʿa al-Raqqī.
rows.anchor: فترى لها في الثاني حسنا لا تراه في الأول . ثم تنظر إليها في قول ربيعة الرقي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Beginning an interrogative with the verb directs denial toward the action itself: its occurrence may be denied, or the action may be presented as improper.
rows.anchor: جملة الأمر أنك تنحو بالإنكار نحو الفعل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A verb-first question can challenge an impossible boast or condemn a proposed action; ‘Shall we compel you when you dislike it?’ exemplifies the latter.
rows.anchor: وعلى ذلك قوله تعالى : ( ﴿ أنلزمكموها وأنتم لها كارهون ﴾ )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Beginning with the noun instead directs denial toward the person as someone capable or disposed to perform the act, rather than denying the act itself.
rows.anchor: فإن بدأت بالاسم فقلت : أأنت تفعل ؟ أو قلت : أهو يفعل ؟

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Starting with the noun directs denial at the identity or status of the alleged actor, rather than at the action itself.
rows.anchor: وجملة الأمر أن تقديم الاسم يقتضي أنك عمدت بالإنكار إلى ذات من قيل إنه يفعل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘Would he kill me while the sword is beside me?’ cannot mean he is incapable of killing: the sword is cited as a means that prevents his action, so the question presumes he could act.
rows.anchor: فذكر ما يكون منعا من الفعل . ومحال أن يقول هو ممن لا يجيء منه الفعل ثم يقول : إني أمنعه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The real force of such interrogatives is to make the hearer reconsider, feel ashamed, desist, or be unable to answer; ‘denial’ is only a label for that effect.
rows.anchor: الذي هو محض المعنى أنه لتنبيه السامع حتى يرجع إلى نفسه ، فيخجل ويرتدع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Questions about impossible acts are figurative rebukes: they compare a person's boast or hope to an absurd impossibility, rather than assert that anyone expects it literally.
rows.anchor: لا يقرر بالمحال ، وبما لا يقول أحد : إنه يكون إلا على سبيل التمثيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With innamā, exclusivity falls on whichever of subject or object is delayed: ‘ʿAmr struck Zayd’ singles out the striker, while ‘ʿAmr struck Zayd’ with the object delayed singles out the one struck.
rows.anchor: فكذلك يقع مع ' إنما ' في المؤخر منهما دون المقدم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In al-Farazdaq's line, the intended exclusivity is that he alone, or someone like him, defends the clan's honor, not that he defends only their honor.
rows.anchor: ذاك لأن غرضه أن يخص المدافع لا المدافع عنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The detached pronoun is necessary to place the delayed subject after the object and secure the intended focus; it is neither grammatical redundancy nor metrical necessity.
rows.anchor: وجملة الأمر أن الواجب أن يكون اللفظ على وجه يجعل الاختصاص فيه للفرزدق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The positive exclusive clauses ‘it is only a reminder and clear Qurʾān’ and ‘it is only revelation’ reinforce the preceding denials that the Prophet was taught poetry or speaks from whim.
rows.anchor: فإثبات ما علمه النبي وأوحي إليه ذكرا وقرآنا تأكيد وتثبيت لنفي أن يكون قد علم الشعر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The distinction between joining and separating clauses is especially subtle; merely calling a clause without a conjunction a fresh start does not explain the choice.
rows.anchor: علم هذا الباب أغمض وأخفى وأدق وأصعب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although God’s response to ‘We are only mockers’ might seem to call for conjunction, it is separate because the first clause quotes the hypocrites while the next is God’s own report of requital.
rows.anchor: كان العطف ممتنعا لاستحالة أن يكون الذي هو خبر من الله تعالى معطوفا على ما هو حكاية عنهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the cited poem, a definite predicate is fronted, but the meaning shows it is intended as delayed; otherwise its initial position would make it the subject.
rows.anchor: وإنما دل على أنه ينوي التأخير المعنى ، ولولا ذلك لكانت المعرفة إذا قدمت هي المبتدأ

words: قُلِ ٱدْعُوا۟ ٱللَّهَ أَوِ ٱدْعُوا۟ ٱلرَّحْمَٰنَ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the verse, ادعوا means call Him by a name, as one says someone is called Zayd or the amir; it does not mean supplicate to two beings.
rows.anchor: ليس المعنى في ' ادعوا ' الدعاء ، ولكن الذكر بالاسم كقولك : هو يدعى زيدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The omitted wording is ‘call Him Allah or call Him al-Raḥmān’; the selector أي requires alternatives, so a literal reading risks wrongly positing two objects of worship.
rows.anchor: وأن في الكلام محذوفا ، وأن التقدير : قل أدعوه الله ، أو ادعوه الرحمن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because wording can be interpreted through different implicit structures without changing its words, sound interpretation requires rhetorical knowledge; a surface reading here could lead to shirk.
rows.anchor: وهو الذي وسع مجال التأويل والتفسير ، حتى صاروا يتأولون في الكلام الواحد تأويلين أو أكثر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Unlike fa, thumma, and aw, wāw adds no sequence, delay, or alternative; it only joins elements under the grammatical relation they share.
rows.anchor: وليس للواو معنى سوى الإشراك في الحكم الذي يقتضيه الإعراب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Coordinated clauses need a meaningful relation: saying Zayd stands and ʿAmr sits presumes that ʿAmr is connected to Zayd and that the listener cares to learn his state too.
rows.anchor: ليس منه بسبب ولا هو مما يذكر بذكره ويتصل حديثه بحديثه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joining a clause unrelated to its predecessor makes the sentence absurd, as in the example of leaving home and then praising a poet with no connection.
rows.anchor: فلو قلت : خرجت اليوم من داري . ثم قلت : وأحسن الذي يقول بيت كذا . قلت ما يضحك منه
